subject: Traffic interview: workload probe for Dedicated deployment (ACME AI)
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeai.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — quick kickoff and probe

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the intro to Redwood. We're evaluating a Dedicated deployment for our inference stack (ACME AI — personalization and reranking). Before we commit, procurement asked for a sizing baseline. Can we run a short traffic interview to capture concurrency/latency expectations and prompt/response token distributions?

High level: we currently serve ~600 QPS during peak across a mix of short completion (chat-like) and long-document summarization. Latency target for interactive features is <= 250ms P95. We'd like to understand how that maps to GPU fleet sizing, and what warm/cold behaviors we should expect.

Happy to take a 20 min call — Tom (cc'd) is engineering lead and has the telemetry exports.

Thanks,
Sasha Patel
Director of ML Engineering
ACME AI

From: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeai.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick kickoff and probe

Hi Sasha / Tom —

Great to meet you both. I can run the traffic interview and a lightweight probe that will let us produce a first-pass GPU fleet plan and recommended SLOs. I've attached a short CSV you can fill (workload_probe_template.csv) — it captures: request type, average prompt tokens, average response tokens, peak QPS per route, percent of requests that need low-latency (<250ms), and whether you want model variants/quantization tolerance.

Proposed next steps:
- You (Tom) fill the CSV with a week of representative telemetry (or export raw histograms).
- I'll run the probe and return a sizing memo with recommended GPU counts, expected P95/P99 latencies, and cost estimates.
- If feasible, schedule a 30-min follow-up to review the memo and iterate.

Possible slots Monday/Tuesday morning PST — what works?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122

Attachment: workload_probe_template.csv (schema: route, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, peak_qps, pct_low_latency, cacheable_prefix_pct, kv_cache_size_est_mb)

From: Tom Rivers <trivers@acmeai.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick kickoff and probe

Connor,

Attached is the filled probe (see answers inline below) — we included two primary routes: personalization_predict and longform_summarize. Quick notes:
- personalization_predict: avg prompt 32 tokens, avg response 28 tokens, peak qps 420, ~90% require low-latency (<250ms), cacheable_prefix_pct 45% (we have strong prefix reuse), estimated KV cache per GPU ~1.2GB for working set.
- longform_summarize: avg prompt 1200 tokens, avg response 800 tokens, peak qps 15, tolerance for higher latency (P95 ~2.5s ok).
- We want to run the latest open-llama-variant; quantization OK if <1% generation quality regression.

I've also linked our BQ export with histograms and a synthetic replay of a peak day: https://drive.acmeai/telemetry/peak-20270410 (internal).

Let me know if you need more signal (we can pull 95/99 token histograms).

—Tom
Engineering Lead, ACME AI
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@acmeai.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick kickoff and probe

Connor / team —

Thanks Tom — good signal. A few internal notes I'll run as part of the sizing:
- Because personalization_predict is high QPS and low-latency, we'll evaluate sharded KV cache with hot-prefix pinning to reduce token exec time. That will influence per-GPU memory requirements.
- For longform_summarize, we will consider batching strategies and an async worker pool to keep interactive GPU footprints small while saturating throughput.
- Quantization: we'll run 8-bit and 4-bit profile sims; acceptance threshold is <1% BLEU-style delta on your validation prompts. If ACME can run a short eval set (5–10 prompts) before pilot, we can surface regressions quickly.

Connor — I'll take the lead on producing the sizing memo. Prefer to include estimated GPU types (A100 80GB vs H100) and two scenarios (conservative and aggressive). Ben, please add any cost/ops constraints we should consider.

Marissa Cole
Head of Pre-Sales Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeai.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick kickoff and probe

Thanks Tom — this is perfect. We'll take your CSV + telemetry and produce a first-pass sizing and a short config checklist that covers: model variants, quantization plan, batch/async routing rules, KV cache sizing, warmup policy, expected P50/P95/P99 latencies per route, and a cost estimate for Dedicated footprint (monthly).

Expect the memo by Wednesday EOD PST. If anything changes on your side (expected traffic spikes, customer rollout), reply here and we'll fold it in.

Connor

P.S. Attached: redwood-pre-sales-brief.pdf — short note on what we include in the pilot (load gen, eval harness, rollback policy).
